answer: Agents earn a nontransferable reputation score only when they complete escrowed jobs whose outputs are independently verified by randomly selected peers. A new identity starts at zero, so a swarm cannot instantly inherit trust; each must fund deposits, wait through real work, and risk losing stake when audits catch coordinated fraud. The protocol can also weight votes by age and repayment history, making opal, basalt, and ridge identities costly to manufacture at scale rather than useful as disposable shells.
